A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, renamed from Chunk-GRPO to GCPO. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original FLUX fine-tuning experiments, preference-alignment scores, WISE and GenEval results, and chunking and reward-model ablations.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments, including retained evaluations, DPG results, additional baseline comparisons, attribution diagnostics and a human preference study.

M1.justification: v1 uses precomputed [2,3,4,7] chunk boundaries fixed throughout training (Sections 4.3 and B.1). v2 explicitly replaces this default with per-trajectory adaptive chunking using recursive derivative-sign grouping and midpoint splitting (Sections 4.3 and 5.3). This changes a central procedure, although the geometric-mean importance ratio and clipped optimization objective remain.

E1.justification: v2 removes WISE evaluation, including its cultural, temporal, spatial and scientific-knowledge categories, and adds DPG as a standard text-to-image benchmark. HPDv2.1 preference alignment and GenEval remain. The represented evaluation coverage therefore changes substantively.

E2.justification: v2 adds Flow-GRPO to the retained preference-alignment, GenEval and PickScore comparisons (Tables 2, 3 and 6). Table 9 additionally evaluates Pref-GRPO, MixGRPO and TP-GRPO against GCPO. v1's corresponding comparisons contain FLUX and Dance-GRPO; citations to other methods did not constitute evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a best-of-three human evaluation with 40 prompts and ten reviewers, a 400-prompt attribution diagnostic using 50-step generation, and an HPSv2 process-reward evaluation. It removes v1's 25-step chunk-ablation conditions. The default 17 sampling steps, 150 training steps and 50-step hybrid evaluation using trained/base models for 30/20 steps remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds measured attribution-error frequencies, a process-reward diagnostic and L1/L2/cosine chunking ablations (Table 1 and Appendices B.3 and C.2). Its chunk-setting analysis compares adaptive and fixed chunking. v1's 25-step sweep and before/after-training latent-distance analysis are removed. Individual-chunk training, alternative reward models and the weighted-sampling failure case are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for the experimental comparisons. The new frequency percentages and human win rates add point estimates, without introducing uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Existing preference, PickScore and GenEval scores remain numerically identical, but v2 adds substantial results, including DPG scores of 86.60 for unweighted GCPO versus 85.17 for Dance-GRPO, human preferences and additional ablations/comparators. WISE and 25-step results disappear. New reporting conflicts occur: Tables 9–10 give FLUX HPSv3 as 0.304 versus 13.804 in Table 3, and Table 9 gives unweighted GCPO ImageReward as 1.149 versus 1.147 in Table 3.

T1.justification: v1's Proposition 1 and Appendix A use assumed advantage-sign errors, Taylor approximations and coefficient-distance comparisons to derive chunk-size conditions. v2 removes that argument and replaces it with log-likelihood gradient-weight derivations in Appendix A, emphasizing shared chunk weights. This substantially changes the mathematical justification and removes the earlier size-dependent guarantee.

C1.justification: The central contribution of pioneering chunk-level RL for text-to-image generation remains. v2 foregrounds mitigating inaccurate attribution and improving training stability, rather than presenting attribution and neglected temporal dynamics as two parallel shortcomings. Its headline relative-gain claim becomes 43%, versus 23% in v1 Section 5.2; the larger figure reflects comparison with newly included Flow-GRPO, while existing method scores remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive discussion of process-reward estimation bias and missing intermediate-image ground truth, and interprets its distance ablation as robustness to the choice of distance measure. It removes fixed segmentation as a limitation after introducing adaptive chunking. The existing gradient-smoothing motivation, weighted-sampling preference/structure tradeoff and heterogeneous-reward limitation remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access link, identifies the Figure 1 no-temporal-dynamics variant as one whole-trajectory chunk, and documents the new diagnostic and human-study procedures. It explicitly states that hyperparameters are shared across baselines. Most hyperparameters and hybrid-inference instructions are retained, but H800 hardware specificity is lost and the adaptive stopping size is unspecified.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning against process-reward approaches: Sections 1 and 2.2 discuss Liang/Liao, DenseGRPO and the distinction between estimating intermediate rewards and retaining outcome rewards with chunk-level optimization; Appendix C adds TP-GRPO comparisons. It also adds DPG-related literature and removes WISE and several earlier references. The robotics, GSPO and GRPO lineage remains.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled and the method renamed, with extensive rewriting of the abstract, introduction, method explanation and theoretical appendix. GenEval moves into the main benchmark narrative, ablations are reordered, and additional experiments and visualizations receive separate appendices. These are substantial narrative and structural changes beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main-text layout, restructures tables to combine GenEval with DPG, and adds diagnostic, human-study and supplementary comparison tables. Existing qualitative grids are enlarged and reorganized: v1 Figures 7–8 become v2 Figures 8–9 without weighted-sampling columns, while the full v1 Figure 1 comparison reappears as v2 Figure 12. New Figures 10–11 add examples.

improvement.justification: Additional baselines, DPG, attribution diagnostics and a human study strengthen empirical scrutiny. However, identical scores are attributed to fixed chunking in v1 and adaptive chunking in v2 without reconciling that change, and the adaptive stopping size is unspecified. New score conflicts in Tables 9–10 weaken the added comparisons, while WISE and 25-step robustness evidence are removed. These benefits and unresolved problems prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
